newsitem.title: THAILAND: Foreign investors' access to Thai gem sector eased.
newsitem.headline: Foreign investors' access to Thai gem sector eased.

text.p: Thailand's Board of Investment (BOI) on Wednesday agreed to lift the requirement that foreign investors have a joint venture partner to invest in several sectors of the local gem and jewellery industry.
The approval was seen as an attempt by the government to promote foreign investment in the industry and promote Thailand as a world centre for gem and jewellery trading.
Thailand is expected to earn more than 63 billion baht ($2.17 billion) from exports of gems and jewellery in 1997, compared to 54 billion baht earned last year.
The BOI said sectors in which full foreign investment would be allowed included precious metals manufacturing and refining, jewellery prototypes and plaster for mold-making.
It said operators would receive corporate income tax exemption for eight years.
However, investors wishing to enjoy these breaks must submit their investment applications by December 31, 1999.
